column2: Act Nine
Dragon Tomb

The Dragon King’s roar rose, and the golden flames rose with it, swiftly kindling the enormous dragon eyes. The dragon spread his wings again. Every scale flared, giving a piercing screech of metal against metal.
The enormous heart that had stopped began to pound like a war drum.
The dragon’s form stretched and writhed once more, as if about to soar into the sky.
After a thousand years of silence, the Dragon King Norton once again towered over the world as its sovereign.
“They’ve... merged!” Caesar said softly.
The Three Gorges Reservoir on the Yangtze, the ancient Kuimen.

On a clear night, ships waiting to pass through the locks lay quietly at anchor. The river was calm, reflecting the light of the stars and moon. A solitary dark figure stood on the shore of a small island in midstream, gazing silently into the distance. The rushing water brought back memories of many years ago.

Many years ago, this little island had been a mountain. From here, one had looked out on Kuimen, seemingly cleft by a god’s ax. In spring everything was green, and a vast wind lifted two people’s white robes.
The dark figure reached toward the water. An ancient incantation traveled across it like the tolling of a bell.

Ripples appeared. Countless bubbles rose from below; wisps of white vapor drifted above the surface. Light like molten steel flowed beneath the water, as though an underwater volcano were about to erupt.

The river boiled. Scalding white vapor shot skyward with a thunderous roar. The surface split. Hundreds of tons of hot seawater surged into the air, then scattered as falling droplets. They struck black scales and swiftly evaporated.
An enormous creature beyond the reach of words.

He broke the surface and lifted his head to the sky, giving a cry like laughter and like a baby’s wail. Then he curved his neck, lowered his head, and met the eyes of the figure on the shore. The portion of his body above water was nearly four stories high. Black scales covered his long neck; serrated black spurs of bone pierced the scales along his spine. An ancient iron mask covered his face, exposing only his uncanny golden eyes.

Without seeing it, no one would have believed such a creature truly existed. His likeness appeared in all kinds of mysterious, heretical books. Some said these creatures hid in caves, holding sulfur in their mouths and breathing fire. Others said they were enormously venomous snakes with more than one head. Still others said they were symbols of heaven’s mandate, half divine. Ancient European sailors whispered that the eastern seas were unnavigable: their waters were red and boiling because magma flowed beneath them, and whole schools of these creatures swam above the molten layer. In their fury they could destroy any great ship, unless you scattered grains of rice. Rice resembled maggots, and the only thing these creatures feared was maggots burrowing beneath their scales.
Yet none of these legends could describe their true appearance.
When he appeared before human beings, he was far more terrible and majestic than any legend.
Only one word could describe them:
“Dragons!”
A long, silent gaze. The dark figure held out a hand. A low, whimpering sound came from the dragon’s mouth. Docilely, he brought his head close and allowed the figure to stroke his nose.
At that moment, the tiny figure and the enormous dragon formed a picture of extraordinary harmony.
“Samson. After two thousand years, we meet again at last,” the figure said softly. “I left you watching the house far too long... Now let’s go home!”
He reached out and caught the iron ring on the dragon’s mask, as though grasping power and dignity once again!

The figure roared at the sky. The dragon roared with him. Their voices intertwined and resonated, carrying far across the river. The dragon’s long tail lashed the water, splitting a rift in its surface. His head traced a perfect arc through the night sky, and he plunged into the rift with the dark figure. Moments later the water closed, leaving only enormous spreading rings.
“What was that?” On a pleasure boat not far from the island, tourists singing outdoor karaoke on the deck all shivered and turned toward the same direction.
They saw only glittering water and black mountains beneath the stars. But the karaoke ended early that night. No one wanted to go on singing.
All night they kept remembering that sound. They did not know what it was, only that it carried a heartbreaking grief.
If it truly was a human voice, what agony, what teeth-grinding anguish, could have produced it?

“It is the night of February thirteenth, 2010, the Chinese lunar Spring Festival. The Moniach is anchored in the Three Gorges Reservoir. The river is quiet, and equipment is functioning normally. Tonight we will carry out Operation Bronze. I am Captain Manstein, and this is my thirteenth captain’s log of the voyage.” Professor Manstein glanced at his watch, dialed an overseas number, switched to speakerphone, and set the phone on the table. “Preparations complete. Board of Trustees, please give us our final orders.”
“Commence the operation. And good luck.” Principal Anjou hung up.
Manstein looked around at everyone. “You all heard. The principal has confirmed.”
Everyone nodded.

“Though we have rehearsed many times, only tonight will you learn all the details. Listen carefully and remember. Success depends on coordination between every team.” Manstein surveyed the students in black combat uniforms standing solemnly in the cabin, hands behind their backs. “Congratulations. This is a real dragon-slaying operation. Here, you will no longer be treated as students. You were chosen for this ship for one reason only: you are the finest of the elite.”

“Hey, could you stop talking so frankly about ‘the finest of the elite’ and forgetting a loser like me, dragged along as expendable backup?” Lu Mingfei grumbled inwardly. He stood behind the others, only half his face showing.

“Unlike last time, the Moniach is fully armed. The Equipment Department has packed its latest creations into the lower hold. This ship embodies humanity’s most advanced technology to date. Its firepower can match a cruiser. No living creature should pose a problem,” Manstein said. “Provided there are no operational errors.”

“This target is more powerful than the one you encountered on campus. Metal and explosions cannot sufficiently harm him, so conventional weapons are ineffective. Allow me to introduce...” Manstein switched on the large screen. An electronic blueprint opened. “Shkval! The world’s fastest torpedo, made in Russia. Its underwater speed reaches two hundred knots, almost as fast as a small airplane. According to our data, dragons can swim at fifty knots, so the target cannot outrun a Shkval torpedo... Lu Mingfei, do you have a question?”
Lu Mingfei raised his hand. “Military magazines say Shkval torpedoes can carry nuclear warheads. Are we planning to use... a nuclear weapon?”
“No. We’ve fitted it with an alchemical warhead!” On the screen, the warhead section enlarged.

“Eight thousand alchemical fragments are embedded in a spiral within the warhead. Their edges are extraordinarily sharp, capable of slicing through dragon scales!” Manstein started an animated demonstration. “Look. When the warhead explodes, the eight thousand fragments open like a metal flower. They spread out and rotate in a plane thirty meters in diameter, like an electric circular saw. But far faster than any saw. It completes a revolution in a few hundredths of a second, completing the cut... and slicing the Dragon King in half!”

“But this is a reservoir, and we’re using... a naval weapon?” Lu Mingfei very much wanted to offer his regards to the parents of the Equipment Department’s lunatics. What if they dropped the torpedo and it sank to the bottom and exploded?

“That’s nothing. The Equipment Department has done things far more outrageous,” Manstein said calmly. “The Three Gorges Reservoir is now a hundred and seventy meters deep. The last underwater earthquake caused roughly two hundred meters of subsidence near the bronze city. At a depth of almost four hundred meters, there’s more than enough room for a Shkval. Even if it hits bottom and explodes, it will merely cause an underwater landslide.”
“What do you mean, ‘merely’? Where does this breezy tone even come from?” Lu Mingfei thought.
But he kept it to himself. Everyone around him wore an expression of perfect calm that said, “Yes. Merely an underwater landslide.”
Live among madmen, and you had to adapt to madmen’s logic.

“We have only one Shkval. One chance to succeed. The underwater team will lure the Dragon King out of the bronze city. Once he enters sonar range, we fire. This is the power of science. Dragons have not yet had time to adapt so quickly. For centuries, humanity has armed itself with science. At last, it can stand on equal terms with alchemy and Yanling,” Manstein said. “Now, the duty roster again. Captain, Manstein. First mate, Grayson, at the helm. Second mate, Gunayal, sonar and torpedoes. Third mate, Pacino, lower hold. Chief engineer, Naoki Kumagai, engines and fuel supply. Underwater operations: Team A, Caesar and Zero. Team B, Chen Motong and Lu Mingfei... Does everyone understand their station?”
“Yes!” everyone answered together.

Lu Mingfei had been assigned to the underwater team because of his unexpectedly good performance in dive training. As a child he had lived on the edge of town, always swimming in nearby ponds and feeling for clams. Had he known the test before dive training served a purpose, he would certainly have held something back, rather than actually straining away as instructed and swimming almost a hundred meters underwater before surfacing.

Fortunately there was Caesar, a hero on land and in the water. Supposedly he had been piloting his family’s yacht around the Great Barrier Reef to study marine life since he was fourteen. Naturally, he ranked first in diving. Zero had surged into second. Lu Mingfei had seen her descend without an air tank, light as a fish, expressionless, as if her face said, “Oxygen is utterly unnecessary for a half-fish creature like me.” Nono ranked third and Lu Mingfei fourth. Team B was the reserve. Unless Team A was finished, Team B needn’t enter the water. And Lu Mingfei had absolute faith in Caesar’s and Zero’s overpowered stats. If even those two couldn’t handle it, the operation was definitely a failure.
Thinking that way made him feel rather safer.
“But I have a problem.” Zero raised her hand. “I can’t enter the water today.”
Lu Mingfei’s head buzzed. Suddenly he had an ominous sense that things were about to go wrong.
“What problem could you possibly have? Relax! You’re perfectly fine! It’s definitely a good time!” Lu Mingfei watched Zero anxiously and nearly said it aloud.
“Not a good time?” Manstein looked Zero up and down. “Are you ill? You look in good condition.”
“Exactly!” Lu Mingfei immediately chimed in. “You look in excellent condition!”
“Aunt Flo’s visiting, so I can’t enter the water.” Zero delivered the sentence with the calm of two hundred degrees below zero.
Lu Mingfei turned to stone on the spot.

God! No way! He had been so attentive to Zero’s health these past days! He had looked after her like a newly sprouted sapling. Whenever she emerged from the water, he had sprinted over with a towel. After dives, he had watched until she finished the thick borscht meant to warm her up. Even wearing a skirt earned a kindly reminder not to catch a chill. If she so much as coughed, he instantly produced a medicine box from his pocket. Everyone thought Lu Mingfei was courting the beautiful Russian girl. He never explained.
For three months, Zero had attended every training session without any significant ailment. Surely Lu Mingfei’s painstaking care deserved some credit.
But when the words “Aunt Flo” emerged from her mouth, Lu Mingfei discovered that women... were something he really did not understand well enough.
“You mean... ‘Aunt Flo’?” he asked carefully. “Do you understand what that means in Chinese?”
“A woman’s menstrual period,” Zero answered.
“Did I hear right? You look fourteen. You get periods? You might as well say you need maternity leave...”
“It is a fact. Menstrual periods are something I have. Furthermore, I am eighteen.” Zero’s cold, hard reply shattered the petrified Lu Mingfei into dust.
“We must still protect women’s basic rights. Team B will substitute,” Manstein said.
“No problem.” Nono nodded.
“Huh?” Lu Mingfei abruptly turned and stared straight at Nono. “You aren’t on your period too, by any chance?”
Nono slapped his forehead, her face darkening. “None of your business! It’s not that time for me!”
“If you’re that scared, Caesar and I can dive together.” Nono withdrew her hand and spoke lightly.
Lu Mingfei froze. The words “Sounds good” had been on his lips, but somehow he swallowed them. He lowered his head, scratched it, and said nothing.

“No,” Manstein said. “Nono cannot dive with Caesar. First, Executive Department rules prohibit personal romantic attachments between dive partners. Second, you’ve already completed hundreds of coordination drills with Lu Mingfei. Switching to Caesar at the last moment would create coordination problems.”
“But do you think he’ll be any use down there like this?” Nono pointed at Lu Mingfei.
“I think he looks in excellent condition,” Zero said.
“Could you at least wait a little before taking revenge?” Lu Mingfei thought.

“I think he looks in excellent condition too,” Manstein said. “Actually, Mingfei’s training results have been quite good. He’s very enthusiastic. Everyone is frightened on their first mission, but he’s S-rank. This shouldn’t be a problem for him.”
“Anyway, follow me down or don’t. I’m fine either way.” Nono patted his shoulder. “I can go alone. It’s only planting bombs to lure out the Dragon King.”
Everyone’s eyes converged on Lu Mingfei.

He looked around. Nono had turned to the porthole, her face blank. She had been like this since he first met her. This girl seemed never to be nervous, never to worry, never really to care about anything.
Whatever he said, yes or no, Nono’s attitude probably wouldn’t change, Lu Mingfei thought.
“Fine. I’ll dive,” he said.
“Mm. Let’s change into our dive suits,” Nono said lightly.
Exactly as he had expected: that same casual tone.

Sitting on the rail, Lu Mingfei looked up at the starry sky. He was about to descend into the water and become a hero. Suddenly the world seemed so lovely, the stars so brilliant. How he wanted to stay here and breathe a little more fresh air...
“Remember. Whatever happens, stay behind me. I’m the team leader. You’re the team member. Understood?” Nono turned to him.
“Got it.” Lu Mingfei looked miserable.
“Watch your oxygen gauges. You have roughly three hours, which should be enough,” Manstein instructed them, crouching by the rail.

“The data cable also serves as a lifeline. Its outer layer is a nanomaterial; ordinarily, it won’t break. If you lose consciousness, we’ll haul you back with it.” Manstein tugged the black cable attached to Lu Mingfei’s dive suit.

“The suits are specially made, fully sealed, able to withstand twenty atmospheres. Their surfaces are nanomaterial, but take care not to tear them. If they spring a leak, you won’t just lose oxygen. The pressure difference will be terrifying.” Manstein patted both their shoulders.
“May I ask something?” Lu Mingfei said tremulously. “We’re going into the Dragon King’s home to plant bombs... If he notices... I imagine he won’t be happy... What do we do?”

“You can rest easy on that point. Operation Bronze was devised by the principal and the entire faculty. We’ve done extensive research and believe the Dragon King will not wake, because he still needs time to regenerate his body.”
“Regenerate his body?” Lu Mingfei blinked.

“Dragon bones are highly malleable, which allows them to imitate humans. Even their dragon forms have different variants. But to use the ultimate Yanling, they must possess an enlarged body. A human body cannot withstand that power. The dragon you saw on campus was forced to break out of his egg when incubation stopped unexpectedly. That was why he couldn’t control his power. He displayed less than one percent of his true strength. If this Dragon King wants to command the ultimate form of fire Yanling, he must form an egg again and grow an enlarged body. He won’t wake readily. That’s why we must use bombs to force him to hatch early.”
“What is the ultimate form of fire Yanling?” Lu Mingfei asked.

“Yanling: Torch Dragon. Serial number one hundred and fourteen. Extremely dangerous. Effects unknown. The Dragon King will certainly want to master it, because he wants revenge... on the entire world.” Manstein stood. “That is precisely why we must kill him before he takes that revenge!”
“Good luck!” Manstein pushed both their shoulders at once, tipping them over the rail into the water.
The spotlights penetrated less than five meters into the river. Before Lu Mingfei lay dense, dark-green water, turbid and full of suspended matter.

The water pressure made his eardrums feel ready to split. The pressure gauge showed they had descended fifty meters. A high-pressure helium-oxygen mix flowed into their suits, helping them resist the external pressure and puffing them up like Michelin Men.

“Breathe deeply, or the pressure really will rupture your eardrums.” Nono’s voice came through his headset. “Stop being so timid. It’s only fifty meters. There’s a freediver who can go down over a hundred, and you’ve even got an air tank.”
“Over a hundred meters without scuba gear? Wouldn’t he suffocate?” Lu Mingfei gulped air, and his ears felt a little better.

“He says diving deep feels like going to another planet. It’s utterly quiet. Everything in the world is far away,” Nono said. “That loneliness is more frightening than suffocation. That’s why the Executive Department requires deep dives to be made in pairs.”

Lu Mingfei paused. Only now did he understand why a mission one person could do had to be carried out by two. He tried imagining Nono absent, with nothing around him but endless dark-green water, and couldn’t help shivering a little.
“We’ve reached the designated position. We’re entering the fissure below,” Nono said. “Hold on to me. Let yourself sink.”

A fissure opened beneath their feet. Holding hands, they relaxed and let the heavy lead weights on their belts draw them slowly down. Uneven rock walls hemmed them tightly in. Lu Mingfei looked up. Pitch-black. The pressure continued to rise. The gauge showed eighty meters, meaning they had descended another twenty since entering the fissure, about the height of eight stories.
“Here,” Nono said softly.
Lu Mingfei raised his head to aim the spotlight ahead.

He saw a wall, an enormous wall stretching endlessly left, right, up, and down. Under the spotlight it shone an ancient blue-green. Mottled verdigris coated it like cotton wool. Nameless plants grew in the foamy corrosion, slender filaments waving gently in the current.
Lu Mingfei drew a deep breath. The outer wall of the bronze city. This thing was nothing short of a miracle.
“It’s been buried here for over a thousand years, right? Who’d ever have found it without the earthquake?” he marveled.
“The presence of something like this in the rock created a stress plane during the earthquake. The fissure followed that exact line,” Nono said.
“There’s a face here!” Lu Mingfei reached out to touch the face rising slightly from the bronze wall. Its features were agonized and hideous, a burning piece of wood held in its mouth.

“A living spirit. You’ll understand once you take Alchemical Biology,” Manstein’s voice said through the headset. “Holding burning wood in its mouth means it is imprisoned by the power of fire, suffering without release. Of the Four Monarchs, the Dragon King Norton is the strongest alchemist. He controls the element of fire, so he can scorch metal with the purest flame, ‘kill’ it, remove impurities, then bring it back to ‘life.’ This is called ‘regenerated metal.’ It has extremely powerful properties and can imprison souls. This is an imprisoned soul. It guards the gates of the bronze city according to the Dragon King’s will.”

“Nono, the vacuum tube you’re carrying contains one milliliter of the Key’s blood. Apply it to the living spirit’s lips. That highly pure dragon blood will open the entrance for you,” Manstein continued.
Nono took the vacuum tube from behind her waist and drew a blood sample with a syringe.
“Is this guy still alive?” Lu Mingfei asked.
“Dead. ‘Living spirit’ is only an alchemical definition. Its consciousness has already died,” Nono said.
“But he...” Lu Mingfei’s voice shook. “Bit me!”
Nono looked up sharply. Lu Mingfei’s hand was caught in the living spirit’s mouth. It really did look as though he had been bitten. He was struggling to pull free.
“Stop moving! It’s only stuck. Living spirits don’t move without good reason. It’s just a lock. Do keyholes bite?” Nono said. “Who told you to touch everything?”
“No... That’s not it!” Lu Mingfei said. “He really bit me!”
His face was white.
Suddenly Nono fell silent. Before her eyes, the bronze face moved. The whole face pushed out of the wall, its corrosion cracking. Sharp canine teeth snapped open and shut with a crunch.
It... really had bitten Lu Mingfei!

The pain felt like having blood drawn at a hospital. His dive glove had split. Countless bubbles streamed through the tear, and the pressure inside his suit plummeted. Unable to speak, he could only stare wide-eyed at the whirling pressure gauge. He wasn’t that expert who could freedive a hundred meters. His lungs were now full of helium-oxygen mixture at several atmospheres of pressure. Once the pressure inside the suit vanished, the gases dissolved in his blood would race to become bubbles.
Could you imagine what someone looked like with blood vessels full of bubbles?
The greatest danger in diving: gas embolism!
Nono immediately reached for him. Whatever had made the living spirit bite him, the priority was to free his hand and seal the tear before the gas in his oxygen cylinder escaped.
A deep, thunderous boom passed straight into her mind, as though someone were reciting an ancient spell in a dark palace.
“Draconic?” Nono’s eyes widened.
The silver vacuum tube slipped from her hand and plunged downward.
“Damn!” she cried.
There were only two samples of the Key’s blood. The backup was still aboard the Moniach.

Beside her, Lu Mingfei was still struggling furiously. In the spotlight, his teeth were clenched, his cheek muscles bulging, his eyes bloodshot. Flailing with all his strength, he looked as though he couldn’t last much longer.
“Pull your hand out! Don’t be afraid!” Abandoning the sample, Nono caught his wrist and hauled. “Bear it! Even if your wrist breaks, get your hand out!”
She was far more experienced underwater than he was. A continuing leak could kill him. A broken wrist could be treated once they surfaced.
“Ow, ow, ow!” Lu Mingfei yelled.

Nono ignored him. Bracing her feet against the bronze wall, she gritted her teeth and pulled with all her strength. His hand jerked free. Losing her balance, she crashed into him. Her first act was to clamp his wrist tightly, stopping any further loss of oxygen.
“How are you?” She shook him hard.
“Oh... Okay,” Lu Mingfei said.
Nono froze. “Okay?”
Lu Mingfei scratched his head. “He... suddenly stopped biting.”
Puzzled, Nono examined the torn glove. His injured finger poked out through the split.
“Scream, scream, scream! Are you the Princess and the Pea?” Suddenly furious, Nono elbowed him in the chest.

There was only a cut less than a centimeter long on his finger, about as deep as a nick from a pencil sharpener’s blade. The living spirit’s wolflike fangs seemed guilty of bluffing. They had stopped as soon as they broke his skin.
“A dead head bit me! Of course I was nervous. I thought it wanted to eat me!” Lu Mingfei protested. Once his suit was sealed at the wrist, the pressure returned and he felt better at once.

Busy squabbling, neither noticed that the living spirit beside them was doing more than simply ceasing to bite Lu Mingfei. Its mouth opened wider and wider. No one who hadn’t seen it would believe a “person” could open their mouth so far, unless they had no jawbone and a mouth built like a giant snake’s, capable of swallowing an elephant.
Nono turned. What she saw was a huge black mouth, as if it meant to... eat them.
Darkness filled her vision. Instinctively, she tightened her hold on Lu Mingfei’s wrist. A whirlpool swept them both inside.
When she opened her eyes again, they were surrounded by air. Nono got up from the ground and looked around.

Before her stretched a bronze corridor lined with countless bronze statues: people in ancient robes and headdresses, civil officials or military commanders holding ivory court tablets. The difference was that long, slender snake necks emerged from their collars and armor. All these officials had cobra-like heads. Comically, some of the snakes even wore hats.
“Wow. Are we dead?” someone beside her asked.
“Nonsense. Could you talk if you were dead?” Without thinking, Nono swung a hand and smacked him.
Lu Mingfei rubbed his head. “I’ve never died. How would I know whether you can talk afterward?”
“Other people might not talk after they die. You’d definitely still be a chatterbox.” Nono reached over and shut his oxygen-cylinder valve, then her own.

“Save a little oxygen. I don’t know whether we can breathe the air here.” She experimentally opened the valve on her helmet’s faceplate. Air smelling of verdigris flowed in, but it wasn’t particularly choking.
“Chen Motong! Lu Mingfei! What’s wrong? What happened?” Manstein’s voice came through their headsets.

They turned to look at the black cable serving as both communication line and lifeline. It hadn’t broken. Instead, it miraculously disappeared into the bronze wall behind them. Nono crouched and felt around it. The wall fit seamlessly against the cable, as if it had been cast around it.

“Chen Motong reporting. A minor accident, but we’re inside the bronze city. Neither of us is injured. Lu Mingfei’s suit is torn, but he still has oxygen,” Nono said. “The only problem is that our communication cable is embedded in the wall.”

“We learned from last time. You’re both carrying extension adapters. Check your pockets.” Manstein breathed easier. “Once the living spirit identifies the blood sample, it opens the entrance. After you enter, the door disappears. That wall is made of regenerated metal, extremely ductile, as malleable as modeling clay. Your communication cable will stay caught until the door opens again.”
Lu Mingfei and Nono found the extension-cable reels in their pockets. They disconnected the black cable from their suits and inserted the extensions.
“Calling Moniach. Do you read?” Nono said.
“Signal clear. No problems,” Manstein replied immediately.

“Two things differ from our predictions. First, when Ye Sheng and Aki came here, years of metal oxidation had depleted the oxygen, making the air unbreathable. Now we can breathe it normally. Second, the door opened before I had time to use the Key’s blood,” Nono said.

“I can probably answer the first question,” Manstein said. “The air is breathable now because the Dragon King has returned to his palace. He’s a reptile and breathes oxygen too. Naturally, his home contains it. In other words, he’s somewhere near you right now.”
Nervously, Lu Mingfei looked around. “Professor, you said he wouldn’t wake, right?”
“He won’t. Growing an enlarged body amounts to incubating all over again. The Dragon King should currently be in an ‘egg.’”
“I can answer the second question.” Lu Mingfei raised his hand. “The living spirit opened the door because... it drank my blood. It felt like having a blood sample drawn at the hospital.”

Manstein was silent for a long time. “The only explanation is your dragon bloodline. Possibly its purity. Highly pure dragon blood. The Key’s Yanling can open every door in the world, but he used his own blood to open the ancient bronze city. Bloodline advantage, not Yanling power.”
“We’re ready. Continuing forward,” Nono said.

“Place the bomb as close as possible to the Dragon King’s bedchamber. Its explosive force is modest, but the alchemical agents inside will trigger a violent chain reaction with water and metal, rapidly exhausting the air in the bronze city. The incubating Dragon King will feel himself suffocating and be forced to break out early. He’ll be extremely weak, and the Shkval can finish him easily.”
“Understood. But first we have to find our way,” Nono said. “There’s a corridor ahead, with many snake-faced statues on either side.”

“The Path of the Sanctuary,” Manstein said. “It’s described in the Ice Sea Fragments. In the age of dragon supremacy, ancient people coming before the Dragon King as his subjects had to follow this path. A bronze palace in northern Europe has an identical one. The snake-faced statues represent the metallic elements under the Dragon King’s command. Eighty-eight in all, according to the alchemical table of elements.”
“Is there a map?” Nono asked.

“There’s an easier way. Remember your introductory alchemy course? In alchemy, the pentagram represents five elements. The lower-right point is fire. This bronze city was also built on alchemical principles, rather like ancient Chinese feng shui. The Dragon King’s bedchamber will be in the lower part of the city. Look for water beneath your feet.”
“There is.” Nono and Lu Mingfei were standing in knee-deep water.
“Water flows from high ground to low. The Ice Sea Fragments say that following the water leads to the throne of flame. Lu Mingfei, use the dye you brought,” Manstein said.
Lu Mingfei pulled the dye tube from his suit pocket, snapped it open, and emptied it into the water.
The fluorescent yellow dye formed a vast yellow-green patch. Moments later, a fine yellow-green thread quietly slipped away along the bottom, like a clever little snake.
“Now that’s high-tech!” Lu Mingfei marveled.

Apparently this bald Manstein knew an extraordinary amount about dragons, greatly improving their mission’s chances. As the saying went, one lousy soldier was one lousy soldier; a lousy general made a whole army lousy. It didn’t matter if Lu Mingfei was lousy. As long as Manstein wasn’t, there was hope.
Nono patted his shoulder. “Follow that line. You lead.”
“We go together!” Lu Mingfei glanced at the snake-faced statues and shook his head.

He hated snakes most of all. Just thinking of them made him feel their cold, slippery bodies, dangerous and venomous. He hated snakes dressed up like respectable people even more. Though these snake-faced figures were all slightly bent at the waist, leaning forward as if bowing, looking like well-educated snakes.
Helplessly, Nono caught his wrist. “Together! If you’re this cowardly, how exhausting is looking after you going to be?”
Side by side, they passed among the snake-faced figures.
After their splashing footsteps faded, the silent corridor filled with the sound of machinery moving and metal scraping.
The snake-faced figures, which had been bowing all along, straightened in unison and stared ahead, cold silver light glinting in their silver-cast eyes.
Lu Mingfei did not know that these snake-faced figures did not, in fact, always bow.
A long trek. The line of dye guided them through the bronze city’s labyrinth of corridors, until they reached an open space.
Water from the corridors emptied into a lake here. The water was so deeply blue it was almost black, cold to the bone and of unknown depth.

Lu Mingfei tilted his head up to shine his helmet light overhead. He saw a bronze ceiling like the vault of heaven, an immense tree growing from its center, transforming into endless varieties of leaves and petals. It resembled a gigantic fractal, dizzying even at a glance.
“This is where Ye Sheng and Aki came. Remember that picture?” Nono asked softly.
“You might as well say it’s where they died.” Lu Mingfei was frightened. “This place is bad luck.”
“We have you, our little map-deciphering ace.” Nono patted his shoulder. “We’ll be fine.”
She shone her light on the water. The dye line was still moving slowly toward the middle of the lake. But once it reached the center, it stopped advancing, as though something were blocking it.
“The water doesn’t flow here?” Lu Mingfei muttered. “Then this is the end. Let’s drop the bomb and run!”
“Wait. Look at that.” Nono aimed her light ahead.

An enormous snake-faced statue sat upright against the bronze wall. Entirely unlike the others, it was a full twenty meters high, like a god in an ancient Greek temple. Even at this distance, Lu Mingfei and Nono had to look up at it like pilgrims.

“If those other statues represent different metallic elements,” Nono said softly, “this should be their master, the Dragon King Norton himself. Look closely. His design is different. Notice the patterns on his arms. That’s Draconic too, symbols that summon power like Yanling. Medieval stories about secret patterns on witches’ bodies refer to things like this.”
“I told you we’d arrived. Take out the bomb, plant it, and let’s go! What, do you want to swim over and carve ‘Nono was here’ on him?” Lu Mingfei said.
“Exactly.” Nono kicked him in the butt, sending him into the water, then dived in herself. Without giving him a say, she caught him and kept him from swimming ashore. “Let’s swim over and look.”
He had no choice. She dragged him toward the center, all the way to where the dye line stopped advancing.
“Look at the line.” Nono put on her faceplate and submerged.
Lu Mingfei copied her. Now he understood why she had insisted on bringing him to the center. The dye hadn’t stopped. On reaching the middle, it had turned straight down.

“The current goes down here. There must be a drain below. Remember the map of the bronze city you deciphered? Straight down was an exit. Ye Sheng and Aki should have passed the bedchamber on the way,” Nono said.

“The bedchamber isn’t here?” Lu Mingfei surfaced and looked at the towering snake-faced statue. “Look. The owner’s statue is right there. This ought to be the bedroom. Like, the room with the wedding picture is the bedroom... Yes, my guess makes sense!”

“Get lost!” Nono said. “No stupid jokes right now. This is where ancient people came to worship the Dragon King. It’s described in the Ice Sea Fragments: they entered on wooden rafts and saw an enormous bronze emperor seated beneath the vault of heaven. It must mean this. But this isn’t the real bedchamber. It’s a temple, a place to create an idol for worship. No record says anyone ever saw the Dragon King himself.”

“Isn’t he tiresome? Living in a huge house is one thing, but he needs a temple and a bedchamber.” His hope of planting the bomb and leaving immediately dashed, Lu Mingfei said dejectedly, “What’s in the bedchamber? Him and his darling little she-dragon?”
“You should find an ‘egg’ in the bedchamber.” Manstein’s voice.
“A dragon egg? Will it be a big guy?” Lu Mingfei was curious.
“Big guy?” Manstein reflected. “Oh, you mean ‘quiet’? Yes. Very quiet. It isn’t time to hatch yet.”
“You can even make sense of that... I bow to you!” Lu Mingfei said.
“Dive! You can’t catch tiger cubs without entering the tiger’s den!” Nono pushed his head down.
“When you steal tiger cubs, the mother’s not home! This time the old dragon is home!” Lu Mingfei sighed.

On the Moniach, Manstein’s gaze followed the descent of Nono’s helmet camera. The deep-blue water was exceptionally clear. No suspended matter was visible in the light, much less a single fish. Dead water, without a trace of vitality.
“Aaah!” Lu Mingfei screamed.
“What is it? Answer! Lu Mingfei, answer!” Manstein cried in alarm.
“What are you screaming for? Stop hugging my legs! Find that rabbit-sized scrap of courage!” Nono’s angry voice.
Zero glanced at Caesar. His face was expressionless.
“Let me turn the camera.” Under Nono’s violent suppression, Lu Mingfei seemed a little more normal.

When the image appeared, everyone drew a deep breath. The bottom was covered in ghastly white bones, so densely packed there was scarcely room to put a foot down. The distinctive skulls and sternums showed that they were human. Thousands upon thousands had died here; their bones had lain for over a thousand years.
“I said plant the bomb and leave! You had to dive. Now we’ve dived into a graveyard!” Lu Mingfei complained.

“Wow, it’s so scary! Skeletons everywhere! Close your eyes. Don’t open them. Let your big sis hold your little hand?” Nono said. “Pah! What’s scary about bones? They’ve soaked here for thousands of years. Are they going to come back to life?”
“That makes sense, but please, as a lady, shouldn’t you shriek a few times at dead people’s bones?” Lu Mingfei said. “You’re as calm as a forensic pathologist!”
“You’ve already shrieked for me. Thank you!”
Nono crouched on the bottom, rummaging through the bones. She picked up a femur and inspected it, then a sternum. Lu Mingfei could not begin to understand what this girl was thinking.

“Looks like the Dragon King eats people. One eaten for every visitor who comes to pay homage? How many years would it take to accumulate this many bones? He certainly picked them clean.” Lu Mingfei looked around.
“These people were soldiers.” Nono held something she had dug from the bones before him.
A corroded rectangular piece of metal, with faintly visible little holes in all four corners.

“An armor plate. Han-dynasty regulation armor. These plates are called lamellae. Tie them together with hemp cord and you have armor. The workmanship is excellent. It should be regulation issue,” Nono said. “The bottom beneath the bones is full of these. You can grab handfuls. Also, look beside that skeleton.” She turned her light. “That’s a ring-pommel saber, commonly used by Eastern Han soldiers. These people should all be military. Government troops.”
“Imperial troops! Not ‘government troops’!” Lu Mingfei said. “So the Dragon King only ate imperial soldiers? Sounds like he sided with the working people!”
“No constant wisecracks! Think you’re an automatic wisecrack machine?” Nono smacked his forehead. “Thousands of Eastern Han soldiers died here, apparently all at once. A sacrifice? Strange.”
She picked up a sternum and studied it, frowning. Shaking her head, she tossed it aside and picked up another. After examining several, she gave up.
“Not a mark on any of the bones. No way to tell how they died.”
“Leave the archaeology for now. Have you found the entrance below?” Manstein asked.
“I’m standing over it!” Nono said.
Lu Mingfei looked down. Sure enough, the fluorescent yellow dye line disappeared into the heap of bones not far away.
“Clear away the bones. Let’s see where the door is.” As she spoke, Nono moved the bones beneath her feet.
Layer upon layer of white bones. When these people died, they must have been piled on top of one another. Lu Mingfei helped her work, imagining how terrible that scene must have been.
“When these people died... was there water here?” Something suddenly struck him.
Nono frowned and thought. “There should have been. According to the Ice Sea Fragments, the bronze city contained water. That’s why humans came before the Dragon King in boats.”

“But there wasn’t any water here when they died,” Lu Mingfei said. “Think about it. If there had been, they’d have floated until they rotted into skeletons and sank. Before that, the bodies would have drifted apart. But look around. They’re all concentrated right here. That means they were gathered here when they died. Somehow, they all died at once. They can’t have dived down. There were no dive suits then. They’d have suffocated.”
“It was...” Nono shivered slightly. “An attack!”

She shivered because the thought was too appalling. When Norton built his palace in northern Europe, people had regarded him as a god. Yet thousands of soldiers had attacked a god’s domain, like the war in ancient legend that killed the Black King. What a scene that must have been was impossible to imagine. One day two thousand years ago, the water here had dried up. On that extraordinary day, soldiers had stormed the bronze city. Humans attacking a god. The place of pilgrimage had echoed with battle cries. The soldiers had charged toward the bedchamber, met disaster here, and all died in an instant.
“Did anyone break into the bedchamber?” Lu Mingfei asked.
“Good question. We’ll soon find out,” Nono said. “Hold out your hand!”
“What for?” he asked, but obediently extended it.

His glove still bore the tear from the living spirit’s bite. There had been no time to repair it, so he could only keep his fist clenched to prevent the high-pressure gas in his suit from escaping. Nono caught his hand and forced his fingers open. As bubbles streamed out, she pressed his hand to the bottom. His wound touched it directly. The bone-deep cold hurt so much he shuddered.
“What are you doing?” Lu Mingfei cried anxiously.
“Hold me!” Nono grabbed his wrist.
“Huh? Where did this explosive line suddenly come from?” His eyes lit up.
Before he could react, Nono had thrown her arms around him. “Don’t move!”

A tremor came from beneath their feet, like the warning of an earthquake. The whole lake bottom slowly shifted. A long, narrow waterspout appeared above Lu Mingfei’s head, its pointed tail stabbing straight down like an awl. Before he could cry out, the support beneath his feet vanished.
Darkness filled his vision. He fell rapidly, spinning and tumbling.

Now he understood why Nono had held him. Once they cleared away the bones, below them lay another entrance guarded by a living spirit. The lake bottom was a single metal structure. After the spirit drank his blood, the metal plates arranged like a turbine fan shifted. The entrance appeared briefly, creating a waterspout that sucked them both in. Had they not held each other, the backs of their heads might have struck the entrance’s edge.
